newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek seamen end crippling 10-day strike.
newsitem.headline: Greek seamen end crippling 10-day strike.

text.p: Greek seamen ended on Thursday a crippling 10-day strike that stranded hundreds of lorries at ports around the country and caused food and fuel shortages on Aegean islands.

A Panhellenic Seamen's Federation (PNO) official said the group decided to abandon its walkout after all-night negotiations with the government, which offered improved proposals on their demands for better bennefits and measures against unemployment.
"There were all night negotiations and the decision is to end the strike," the official said.
However, Greece's biggest labour confederation, GSEE, went ahead with a 24-hour nationwide walkout on Thursday against a revised taxation system.

The GSEE strike is expected to affect industries, public corporations and transport. Trains and buses will strike all day, while the national carrier Olympic Airaways will stage a three-hour work stoppage mid-day.

Greek Prime Minister Costas Simitis, whose tough economic policies have prompted strong reaction from labour unions, started urgent talks with the seamen late on Wednesday as soon as he arrived from a European Socialists' meeting in Rome.
The seamen's strike had paralysed sea transport, leaving thousands of tonnes of farm produce rotting at ports.
Aegean islands, which depend on ships to survive in the winter, reported shortages in food, fuel and medicine. The Greek nave was called in to deliver emergency supplies.
Scuffles broke out between stranded lorry drivers, farmers and seamen at ports around Greece and coast guard forces intervened to keep them apart.
Other labour groups have also staged walkouts in the past two weeks against the government's tight incomes and tax policies but Simitis has rejected all demands.
High school teachers have been on strike since Monday demanding better pay.
